steps.u: Deploys to Kubernetes cause a few seconds of 503s. Make rollouts zero downtime.

steps.r:
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: shop/web:latest

steps.a: There is no readiness probe, so new pods receive traffic as soon as they start, and no preStop delay, so terminating pods drop in-flight requests while the load balancer is still sending to them. I'll add a readiness probe, a preStop sleep and a rolling update that never removes a pod before its replacement is ready.

i.new_string:
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate: { maxUnavailable: 0, maxSurge: 1 }

image: shop/web:latest
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 8080 }
          periodSeconds: 3
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec: { command: ["sleep", "10"] }

steps.a: Only a server-side dry run so far; I haven't done a live rollout under load to see the 503s disappear.

reference.summary: Changed the Kubernetes deployment toward zero-downtime rollouts: a readiness probe, a preStop delay so terminating pods keep serving while the load balancer drains, and a rolling update with no unavailable pods. Only a server dry run was done, so the effect under load is unverified.
